newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Multinational force secures Albanian port, airport.
newsitem.headline: Multinational force secures Albanian port, airport.

text.p: Heavily armed soldiers from Italy, France and Spain secured two bridgeheads in Albania on Tuesday to begin protecting aid deliveries in the chaotic Balkan nation.
The Albania government warmly welcomed the arrival of nearly 1,200 soldiers in the multinational force and said they could help restore order after weeks of anarchy.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan applauded the start of "Operation Alba", but said the soldiers on the Italian-led mission should leave the disarming of rebels to the Albanian authorities.
"This operation is a humanitarian one to make sure aid gets to the people," he said in Rome.

Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured during the weeks of anarchy and banditry that swept Europe's poorest nation after fraudulent investment schemes wiped out the savings of many families.
Around a million rifles and other weapons were stolen by rebel gangs and ordinary Albanians from armouries left undefended when soldiers and police deserted their posts.
There were no signs on Tuesday of an end to the violence. Police killed an escaped convict in a shoot-out in the south-eastern town of Bilisht after he wounded two officers.
In the northern town of Shkoder, a gunman entered a hospital; and killed a patient while doctors operated on him for bullet wounds from an earlier shooting.
Police forces in Gramsh confiscated three trucks filled with automatic rifles, machine guns and grenade launchers during a raid, Albania's news agency ATA said.
Gramsh, about 100 km (60 miles) south of Tirana, has been a centre for the illegal arms trade after three army depots nearby were emptied and 100,000 Kalashnikov assault rifles were stolen.
Troops landed at Tirana airport and the port of Durres on Tuesday.
"We are here to help Albania in a moment of national difficulty," said Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta, who flew to Durres to observe the landing.

Six Italian military planes carrying 150 paratroopers landed just after dawn at Tirana airport moments before the French troop transport ship Orage, with 450 French soldiers, reached Durres, 40 km (25 miles) west of the capital.
In cold, windy conditions, the French troops unloaded four helicopters, six tanks and dozens of armoured vehicles as the Italian navy flagship Vittorio Veneto patrolled offshore.
A team of 60 French marines had made a sweep of Durres harbour before the landing because of reports there might be a guerrilla attack, French military officials said.

The Italian amphibious assault ship San Marco dropped anchor next to the Orage and 200 Italian troops disembarked. The Spanish ship Hernan Cortes, with 350 Spanish troops on board, followed the Orage into Durres.
Dozens of Albanians watched the troops and equipment unload. Many said the troops were a symbol of hope.
The U.N. World Food Programme plans to distribute aid throughout Albania as soon as possible. A ship with 400 tonnes of wheat, beans and vegetable oil arrived in Durres on Tuesday.
Officials said the country's poor were desperately in need of food and one in 10 Albanians needed humanitarian aid.

French Defence Minister Charles Millon said the Italian-led, which will rise reach 6,000 within three weeks, had a far broader mandate to use arms than that granted to U.N. peacekeepers during the Bosnian war.
But he said the troops would not try to collect weapons.
"This is neither a police mission, nor one to disarm people," he said. Greece, Turkey, Austria, Denmark and Romania are also contributing soldiers to the mission.
